llm.summary: The skill appears to implement RunPod + imgbb media operations (which matches its description), but its manifest and runtime wrapper have inconsistencies and it will upload any local images to a public image host — review secrets handling and the wrapper before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md match the stated purpose: calling RunPod public endpoints to generate/edit/animate media. The requirement for an imgbb key (to convert local files into public URLs) is coherent with the stated functionality. However the top-level registry metadata (presented above) lists no required env vars/credentials while _meta.json and SKILL.md declare two required secrets (/runpod/apiKey and /imgbb/apiKey). This manifest mismatch should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts only call RunPod and imgbb APIs, upload local images to imgbb, poll RunPod jobs, and save output to ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media. They read ~/.openclaw/secrets.json to obtain keys (or use env vars). There are no instructions to read unrelated files or exfiltrate data beyond RunPod/imgbb, but note that any local image passed to the skill is uploaded to imgbb (public URL), so private images would become public.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (scripts are included and executed directly), which lowers install risk. One inconsistency: run.sh execs 'uv run <script>.py' — a binary named 'uv' is not declared in required binaries. If 'uv' is absent the wrapper will fail; if present, it's an undeclared external dependency. No downloads from arbitrary URLs or extract operations are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only secrets required by the code are the RunPod API key and an imgbb API key — both are justified by the skill's purpose. That said, the skill reads ~/.openclaw/secrets.json (the user's centralized secrets file); while it looks up only the declared JSON pointers, having any skill read that file is sensitive. Also the top-level registry incorrectly reported no required secrets — a coherence issue that could confuse users.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent elevated privileges. It writes outputs to ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media and may modify its local endpoints.json when discover_endpoints add is used (this is limited to the skill's own files). It does read the user's secrets.json to obtain API keys (expected for operation).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:
- Confirm and provide only the two required keys: RunPod API key and imgbb API key. The skill will read ~/.openclaw/secrets.json (and/or env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY / IMGBB_API_KEY).
- Be aware: any local image you pass will be uploaded to imgbb and become publicly accessible. Do not use private or sensitive images unless you accept public hosting.
- The published registry metadata is inconsistent: the top-level listing claims no required secrets while _meta.json and SKILL.md require two. Ask the publisher to fix the manifest so required secrets are declared clearly.
- The run.sh wrapper uses an undeclared 'uv' command (exec uv run ...). Verify the runtime invocation works in your environment or edit run.sh to call Python directly (e.g., python3) before running.
- discover_endpoints add will write to the skill's endpoints.json in-place. This modifies the skill directory only, but be comfortable with that behavior.
- Inspect or run the scripts in a controlled environment first (no sensitive images) to verify behavior. If you lack trust in the source (homepage unknown), prefer running in an isolated container or VM.
